lesson.title: Sorting: merge sort from scratch
lesson.note: Divide, conquer, merge — the classic O(n log n) argument, written out.
lesson.code:
def merge_sort(xs):
    if len(xs) <= 1:
        return xs
    mid = len(xs) // 2
    left = merge_sort(xs[:mid])
    right = merge_sort(xs[mid:])
    out, i, j = [], 0, 0
    while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
        if left[i] <= right[j]:
            out.append(left[i]); i += 1
        else:
            out.append(right[j]); j += 1
    out.extend(left[i:]); out.extend(right[j:])
    return out

import random
random.seed(7)
data = [random.randint(1, 99) for _ in range(12)]
print("before:", data)
print("after :", merge_sort(data))
print("stable:", merge_sort(data) == sorted(data))

import Data.List (sortBy, group, sort)

  | m >= 80 = 'B'

  where sieve [] = []
        sieve (p:xs) = p : sieve [x | x <- xs, x `mod` p /= 0]

  putStrLn ("word groups: " ++ show (map (\g -> (head g, length g)) . group . sort $ words "a b a c b a"))

lesson.title: Correlation and a least-squares fit by hand
lesson.note: Both formulas are three lines each once you write them out.
lesson.code:
import statistics as st

attendance = [0.94, 0.81, 0.88, 0.62, 0.91, 0.70, 0.99]
marks      = [91,   78,   84,   65,   88,   72,   95]

def pearson(xs, ys):
    mx, my = st.mean(xs), st.mean(ys)
    cov = sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys))
    return cov / (st.stdev(xs) * st.stdev(ys) * (len(xs) - 1))

def fit(xs, ys):
    mx, my = st.mean(xs), st.mean(ys)
    slope = sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys)) / sum((x - mx) ** 2 for x in xs)
    return slope, my - slope * mx

r = pearson(attendance, marks)
m, c = fit(attendance, marks)

print(f"correlation : {r:.4f}")
print(f"fit         : marks = {m:.2f} * attendance + {c:.2f}")
for a in (0.6, 0.8, 1.0):
    print(f"  attendance {a:.1f} -> predicted {m * a + c:.1f}")

lesson.title: CPU scheduling: FCFS vs shortest-job-first
lesson.note: Same processes, two policies, very different average waiting times.
lesson.code:
jobs = [("P1", 0, 7), ("P2", 2, 4), ("P3", 4, 1), ("P4", 5, 4)]

def simulate(order_key, label):
    time, done, pending = 0, [], sorted(jobs, key=lambda j: j[1])
    ready, queue = [], list(pending)
    while queue or ready:
        while queue and queue[0][1] <= time:
            ready.append(queue.pop(0))
        if not ready:
            time = queue[0][1]
            continue
        ready.sort(key=order_key)
        name, arrival, burst = ready.pop(0)
        start = max(time, arrival)
        done.append((name, start - arrival, start + burst - arrival))
        time = start + burst
    wait = sum(w for _, w, _ in done) / len(done)
    turn = sum(t for _, _, t in done) / len(done)
    print(f"{label}: avg wait {wait:.2f}, avg turnaround {turn:.2f}")
    print("   " + "  ".join(f"{n} w={w}" for n, w, _ in done))

simulate(lambda j: j[1], "FCFS")
simulate(lambda j: j[2], "SJF ")

lesson.title: Producer / consumer with a bounded buffer
lesson.note: The classic synchronisation problem, stepped through one operation at a time.
lesson.code:
from collections import deque

CAPACITY = 3
buffer = deque()
produced, consumed, log = [], [], []

items = [i * i for i in range(1, 8)]
next_item = 0

# One scheduler step: the producer runs when there is room,
# the consumer runs when there is something to take.
for step in range(1, 16):
    if next_item < len(items) and len(buffer) < CAPACITY:
        value = items[next_item]
        buffer.append(value)
        produced.append(value)
        next_item += 1
        log.append(f"{step:2}. produce {value:3}  buffer={list(buffer)}")
    elif buffer:
        value = buffer.popleft()
        consumed.append(value)
        log.append(f"{step:2}. consume {value:3}  buffer={list(buffer)}")
    else:
        log.append(f"{step:2}. both blocked")

print("\n".join(log))
print("\nproduced:", produced)
print("consumed:", consumed)
print("still buffered:", list(buffer))
print("nothing lost:", sorted(consumed + list(buffer)) == sorted(produced))

lesson.title: Number theory: gcd, modular inverse and CRT
lesson.note: Euclid's algorithm underpins most of public-key cryptography.
lesson.code:
def egcd(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        return a, 1, 0
    g, x, y = egcd(b, a % b)
    return g, y, x - (a // b) * y

def inverse(a, m):
    g, x, _ = egcd(a, m)
    if g != 1:
        return None
    return x % m

print("gcd(252, 198)      :", egcd(252, 198)[0])
print("inverse of 7 mod 26:", inverse(7, 26))
print("check 7 * 15 mod 26:", (7 * inverse(7, 26)) % 26)

def crt(pairs):
    total, product = 0, 1
    for _, m in pairs: product *= m
    for r, m in pairs:
        p = product // m
        total += r * inverse(p, m) * p
    return total % product

print("x = 2 mod 3, 3 mod 5, 2 mod 7 ->", crt([(2,3),(3,5),(2,7)]))
print("counting: C(10,3) =", __import__("math").comb(10, 3))

lesson.title: Matrix multiplication and determinants by hand
lesson.note: Write it once yourself and NumPy stops being magic.
lesson.code:
def matmul(A, B):
    return [[sum(A[i][k] * B[k][j] for k in range(len(B)))
             for j in range(len(B[0]))] for i in range(len(A))]

def transpose(M):
    return [list(row) for row in zip(*M)]

def det3(M):
    a, b, c = M[0]
    return (a * (M[1][1]*M[2][2] - M[1][2]*M[2][1])
          - b * (M[1][0]*M[2][2] - M[1][2]*M[2][0])
          + c * (M[1][0]*M[2][1] - M[1][1]*M[2][0]))

A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
B = [[0, 1], [1, 0]]
print("A x B    :", matmul(A, B))
print("A^T      :", transpose(A))

M = [[2, -1, 0], [1, 3, 2], [0, 1, 1]]
print("det(M)   :", det3(M))

def power_iteration(M, steps=40):
    v = [1.0] * len(M)
    for _ in range(steps):
        w = [sum(M[i][j] * v[j] for j in range(len(v))) for i in range(len(M))]
        norm = max(abs(x) for x in w)
        v = [x / norm for x in w]
    return norm, [round(x, 4) for x in v]

val, vec = power_iteration([[2, 1], [1, 2]])
print("dominant eigenvalue:", round(val, 4), "eigenvector:", vec)

lesson.note: Undecidability is a two-line diagonal argument once the setup is clear.
lesson.code:
tape = list("111+11") + ["_"] * 6
rules = {
    ("q0","1"): ("q0","1","R"),
    ("q0","+"): ("q1","1","R"),
    ("q1","1"): ("q1","1","R"),
    ("q1","_"): ("q2","_","L"),
    ("q2","1"): ("q3","_","S"),
}

state, head, steps = "q0", 0, 0
while state != "q3" and steps < 50:
    symbol = tape[head]
    if (state, symbol) not in rules:
        break
    state, write, move = rules[(state, symbol)]
    tape[head] = write
    head += 1 if move == "R" else (-1 if move == "L" else 0)
    steps += 1

print("tape after :", "".join(tape).rstrip("_"))
print("unary sum  :", "".join(tape).count("1"), "(3 + 2)")
print("halted in  :", steps, "steps")

print("\nWhy no program can decide halting:")
print("  suppose halts(p, x) exists.")
print("  define trouble(p): if halts(p, p): loop forever, else: stop.")
print("  now ask: does trouble(trouble) halt?  Either answer contradicts itself.")

lesson.title: k-means clustering from scratch
lesson.note: Assign, recompute, repeat — unsupervised learning in fifteen lines.
lesson.code:
import random, math

random.seed(4)
points = ([(random.gauss(2, 0.4), random.gauss(2, 0.4)) for _ in range(30)] +
          [(random.gauss(6, 0.5), random.gauss(5, 0.5)) for _ in range(30)] +
          [(random.gauss(2.5, 0.4), random.gauss(6, 0.4)) for _ in range(30)])

def dist(a, b): return math.hypot(a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1])

centres = random.sample(points, 3)
for step in range(12):
    groups = [[] for _ in centres]
    for p in points:
        groups[min(range(len(centres)), key=lambda i: dist(p, centres[i]))].append(p)
    new = [(sum(x for x, _ in g) / len(g), sum(y for _, y in g) / len(g)) if g else centres[i]
           for i, g in enumerate(groups)]
    shift = sum(dist(a, b) for a, b in zip(centres, new))
    centres = new
    if shift < 1e-6:
        print(f"converged after {step + 1} steps")
        break

for i, (c, g) in enumerate(sorted(zip(centres, groups)), start=1):
    print(f"cluster {i}: centre ({c[0]:.2f}, {c[1]:.2f})  size {len(g)}")

inertia = sum(dist(p, min(centres, key=lambda c: dist(p, c))) ** 2 for p in points)
print(f"inertia: {inertia:.2f}")

lesson.title: Decision tree splits and information gain
lesson.note: Entropy tells the tree which question to ask first.
lesson.code:
import math
from collections import Counter

data = [
    ("sunny",  "hot",  "high",   False),
    ("sunny",  "hot",  "high",   False),
    ("cloudy", "hot",  "high",   True),
    ("rainy",  "mild", "high",   True),
    ("rainy",  "cool", "normal", True),
    ("rainy",  "cool", "normal", False),
    ("cloudy", "cool", "normal", True),
    ("sunny",  "mild", "high",   False),
    ("sunny",  "cool", "normal", True),
    ("rainy",  "mild", "normal", True),
]
FEATURES = ["outlook", "temp", "humidity"]

def entropy(rows):
    counts = Counter(r[-1] for r in rows)
    total = len(rows)
    return -sum((c / total) * math.log2(c / total) for c in counts.values())

def gain(rows, index):
    base = entropy(rows)
    groups = {}
    for r in rows:
        groups.setdefault(r[index], []).append(r)
    weighted = sum(len(g) / len(rows) * entropy(g) for g in groups.values())
    return base - weighted

print(f"base entropy: {entropy(data):.4f}\n")
for i, name in enumerate(FEATURES):
    print(f"  split on {name:9} -> gain {gain(data, i):.4f}")

best = max(range(len(FEATURES)), key=lambda i: gain(data, i))
print(f"\nroot of the tree: {FEATURES[best]}")

lesson.title: A neural network with backpropagation, no framework
lesson.note: Forward pass, loss, chain rule, update — that is all a framework does.
lesson.code:
import math, random

random.seed(1)

X = [(0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1)]
Y = [0, 1, 1, 0]                      # XOR: not linearly separable

def sigmoid(x): return 1 / (1 + math.exp(-x))

W1 = [[random.uniform(-1,1) for _ in range(2)] for _ in range(3)]
b1 = [0.0] * 3
W2 = [random.uniform(-1,1) for _ in range(3)]
b2 = 0.0
lr = 0.6

for epoch in range(1, 6001):
    loss = 0.0
    for (x1, x2), target in zip(X, Y):
        h = [sigmoid(W1[i][0]*x1 + W1[i][1]*x2 + b1[i]) for i in range(3)]
        out = sigmoid(sum(W2[i]*h[i] for i in range(3)) + b2)
        loss += (out - target) ** 2

        d_out = 2 * (out - target) * out * (1 - out)
        for i in range(3):
            d_h = d_out * W2[i] * h[i] * (1 - h[i])
            W2[i] -= lr * d_out * h[i]
            W1[i][0] -= lr * d_h * x1
            W1[i][1] -= lr * d_h * x2
            b1[i] -= lr * d_h
        b2 -= lr * d_out

    if epoch % 1500 == 0:
        print(f"epoch {epoch:4}  loss {loss/4:.6f}")

print("\nlearned XOR:")
for (x1, x2), target in zip(X, Y):
    h = [sigmoid(W1[i][0]*x1 + W1[i][1]*x2 + b1[i]) for i in range(3)]
    out = sigmoid(sum(W2[i]*h[i] for i in range(3)) + b2)
    print(f"  {x1} XOR {x2} = {round(out)}  (raw {out:.4f}, target {target})")

lesson.note: The loss every classifier is trained with, written out in full.
lesson.code:
import math

def softmax(zs):
    m = max(zs)
    exps = [math.exp(z - m) for z in zs]
    total = sum(exps)
    return [e / total for e in exps]

logits = [2.0, 1.0, 0.1]
probs = softmax(logits)
labels = ["cat", "dog", "bird"]

print("logits :", logits)
for name, p in zip(labels, probs):
    print(f"  P({name:4}) = {p:.4f}")

target = 0                                   # true class is "cat"
loss = -math.log(probs[target])
print(f"\ncross-entropy loss: {loss:.4f}")

grads = [p - (1 if i == target else 0) for i, p in enumerate(probs)]
print("gradient wrt logits:", [round(g, 4) for g in grads])

lr = 0.5
updated = [z - lr * g for z, g in zip(logits, grads)]
print("after one step     :", [round(z, 4) for z in updated])
print("new P(cat)         :", round(softmax(updated)[0], 4))

lesson.title: Convolution, edge detection and pooling by hand
lesson.note: A kernel sliding over a grid — that is every conv layer, forever.
lesson.code:
image = [
    [10, 10, 10, 80, 80, 80],
    [10, 10, 10, 80, 80, 80],
    [10, 10, 10, 80, 80, 80],
    [10, 10, 10, 80, 80, 80],
    [10, 10, 10, 80, 80, 80],
    [10, 10, 10, 80, 80, 80],
]
sobel_x = [[-1, 0, 1], [-2, 0, 2], [-1, 0, 1]]

def convolve(img, kernel):
    k, n = len(kernel), len(img)
    out = []
    for i in range(n - k + 1):
        row = []
        for j in range(n - k + 1):
            row.append(sum(img[i+a][j+b] * kernel[a][b] for a in range(k) for b in range(k)))
        out.append(row)
    return out

def maxpool(img, size=2):
    return [[max(img[i+a][j+b] for a in range(size) for b in range(size))
             for j in range(0, len(img[0]) - size + 1, size)]
            for i in range(0, len(img) - size + 1, size)]

edges = convolve(image, sobel_x)
print("vertical edge response:")
for row in edges:
    print("  " + " ".join(f"{v:5}" for v in row))

print("\nafter 2x2 max pooling:")
for row in maxpool(edges):
    print("  " + " ".join(f"{v:5}" for v in row))

print("\nstrongest response:", max(max(r) for r in edges), "at the 10 -> 80 boundary")

import random
from collections import defaultdict, Counter

corpus = ("the cache stores pages . the cache is fast . "

lesson.title: Chunking, embedding and retrieval — a RAG pipeline
lesson.note: Split, embed, rank, answer. Every RAG system is these four steps.
lesson.code:
import math, re
from collections import Counter

document = """
A cache stores recently used data so it can be read again quickly.
Cache memory sits between the CPU and main memory.
A pointer holds the address of a value in memory.
Pointer arithmetic moves through an array element by element.
Virtual memory lets a process use more address space than exists physically.
Paging moves fixed-size blocks between disk and main memory.
""".strip()

def chunk(text, size=2):
    lines = [l.strip() for l in text.split("\n") if l.strip()]
    return [" ".join(lines[i:i+size]) for i in range(0, len(lines), size)]

def embed(text):
    return Counter(re.findall(r"[a-z]+", text.lower()))

def cosine(a, b):
    shared = set(a) & set(b)
    num = sum(a[w] * b[w] for w in shared)
    na = math.sqrt(sum(v*v for v in a.values()))
    nb = math.sqrt(sum(v*v for v in b.values()))
    return num / (na * nb) if na and nb else 0.0

chunks = chunk(document)
index = [(c, embed(c)) for c in chunks]
print(f"indexed {len(chunks)} chunks\n")

for question in ["how does paging work?", "what is a pointer?"]:
    q = embed(question)
    ranked = sorted(index, key=lambda pair: -cosine(q, pair[1]))
    print(f"Q: {question}")
    for c, vec in ranked[:2]:
        print(f"   {cosine(q, vec):.3f}  {c[:66]}...")
    print(f"   -> context sent to the model: chunk with score {cosine(q, ranked[0][1]):.3f}\n")
